identity.action: European Commission publicly confirms October AI-assisted cyberattack
identity.dateBasis: Dated 2026-11-19 as a disclosure node (when POLITICO published its exclusive and the Commission publicly confirmed the campaign); explicitly distinguishes Oct 22 initial detection date.
identity.deduplicationReason: Distinct institutional disclosure of an AI-assisted cyberattack against the European Commission.

classification.reason: Core action is public disclosure of an AI-assisted cybersecurity incident targeting a major public institution.

significance.rationale: L1 confirmed institutional incident disclosure backed by two genuinely distinct independent Tier-2 origins (POLITICO Europe exclusive via EU officials/leaked email + Brussels briefing via The Record/DW); lacks published external independent investigation and external remedial actions.
significance.whyNotHigher: Under L2-SAFETY, external_remedial_action and independent_investigation are null while CERT-EU's internal investigation remains open and unpublicized.
significance.whyNotLower: Corroborated by two independent origins and three Tier-2 outlets (POLITICO Europe, The Record, Deutsche Welle).

documented_incident.rationale: POLITICO Europe's exclusive and Commission spokesperson Regnier's Nov 19 confirmation both establish the Oct 22 AI-assisted cyber campaign.

external_remedial_action.rationale: Only the Commission's own internal containment and notifications are confirmed; external third-party remedial actions are not established.

independent_investigation.rationale: Investigation is being handled by EU bodies (CERT-EU and EDPS) and no independent external technical report has been published.

consensus.reason: Public confirmation and prior system disruptions are independently corroborated across two origins; full forensic scope and attribution remain undisclosed.

dispute.reason: No factual dispute over the Commission's confirmation; ARTEX tool use is reported by POLITICO via CERT-EU/officials but not officially named by Regnier.

evidence.quote: Weapon of choice: The EU institutions’ cybersecurity watchdog, CERT-EU, detected earlier this month that international hackers used ARTEX, a publicly available AI-powered tool designed to identify vulnerabilities in IT systems.

Speaking to journalists, Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier said the first signs of the attack were detected October 22. He described the incident as an “AI-generated cyber campaign” but did not identify the tool used or the attackers’ apparent motivation.
The incident was detected on October 22 and there was ‌no evidence ​of a data breach affecting Commission staff as a whole, European Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier told reporters.

Disruption has lasted over 10 days. Sysper, the Commission’s HR platform for payslips, leave requests and timesheets, and MyPMO, its medical reimbursement system, were restored earlier this week — though Sysper briefly crashed again yesterday.
